hook.line: Ladies and gentlemen, today is the day the world will remember.
hook.visual: Man in cap and glasses in a parked car holding a lav mic; a small b-roll window above his head swaps image every ~0.4 s (brain scan, mushrooms, crowds) over word-by-word captions.

beats.what: Grand announcement opener; b-roll window above his head changes almost every word
Names the product: an unrestricted AI model you can install; red glitch skull image above him
ChatGPT and Claude logos flank the inset as he names them
Terminal screenshots beside the inset while he says they added agentic coding
'Drumroll please' on a clean frame with no inset, a beat of pause
List of science models (DNA, proteins, atoms) each paired with an illustration
Product landing page shown: 'The world's first AI that doesn't say No'
Scarcity CTA: first 1,000 people who comment the keyword get access
Signs off 'good night' on a plain frame

why_it_works: Historic-announcement framing ('the world will remember') creates a curiosity gap before the product is named
The b-roll window above his head changes on nearly every phrase, so the eye always has something new while the face stays fixed
Each listed capability gets its own picture, turning an abstract list into a fast slideshow
Comment-a-keyword with a 1,000-person cap adds scarcity and drives comments (480)
weaknesses: Hype tone and 'for research purposes only' disclaimer can read as clickbait
Inset images are small and pass too fast to read
No demo of the product actually working; the 'copy, paste, enter' step is only told
for_robert: Put a small changing picture window above his head that updates on key words; Fred could live in that window and swap props per phrase instead of stock images.
